citations.description: set_baseline always stamps baseline_advanced_at = _now_iso() with no change-guard

findings.criterion: A reconcile pass that changes N bindings produces a bindings.json diff proportional to N, not to the total binding count.
findings.detail: The fix has not been implemented. `_advance_baselines` in reconcile.py (lines 506–522) still iterates ALL confirmed bindings in the current snapshot window and calls `binding_store.set_baseline(local_id, ...)` unconditionally for each one. `set_baseline` in binding_store.py (lines 362–375) still stamps `entry["baseline_advanced_at"] = _now_iso()` on every call, regardless of whether the binding's fields actually changed. This is exactly the root cause described in the ticket: ~1,145 per-binding timestamp updates per pass, producing a diff proportional to the total binding count, not to N changed bindings.
